title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: A sanitary tee is designed specifically to transition flow from a horizontal branch into a vertical stack or vent. Installing a sanitary tee flat on its side in a horizontal drain line is a critical installation error. Because the sweep radius of a sanitary tee is short, horizontal solids lack the momentum needed to clear the junction smoothly. This causes waste accumulation, frequent clogs, and improper drainage flow. For horizontal-to-horizontal transitions, plumbing codes require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep wye to ensure smooth directional movement of waste.
